title: CppCon 2019: Matt Godbolt “Path Tracing Three Ways: A Study of C++ Style”
summary: Matt Godbolt builds a toy path tracer in C++ in three different styles and compares them on clarity, testability, compile time and run-time performance. The talk was given at CppCon 2019.
why: HN points to it as a concrete demonstration of object-oriented versus cache-friendly design and the performance effects of branch misprediction.

categories.name: C, C++, Rust, Go & systems languages

quote.text: On OOP versus more cache friendly approaches and branch prediction this talk from CPPCon 2019 is great
